drug_class: Uric acid reducer (PEGylated recombinant uricase enzyme)
purpose: Pegloticase is used to treat severe, long-lasting gout in adults when other medicines have not worked well enough. Gout causes painful swelling in your joints due to a buildup of uric acid in your body. This medicine helps bring your uric acid levels down to a safe range.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes an enzyme that breaks down uric acid, but sometimes it cannot keep up with the amount your body produces. Pegloticase is a man-made version of that enzyme, given through an IV, that breaks down uric acid much more efficiently. Think of it like a cleanup crew that goes through your bloodstream and clears out the excess uric acid that is causing your gout flares.
common_side_effects: Gout flares (especially in the first few months of treatment), nausea, bruising, sore throat, constipation, chest pain, and vomiting. Infusion reactions like flushing, redness, rash, or shortness of breath during or shortly after the IV infusion are also common.
warnings: There is a serious risk of infusion reactions and severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis), so you will always be given pre-medications beforehand and monitored closely during and after your infusion. People with a certain enzyme deficiency called G6PD should not use this medicine because it can cause dangerous destruction of red blood cells. Your doctor will check your uric acid levels regularly — if your levels rise, the medicine will likely be stopped to reduce your reaction risk. Do not take allopurinol or febuxostat while using pegloticase.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 8 mg given as an IV infusion over at least 2 hours, once every 2 weeks, at a clinic or infusion center. You will be given antihistamines and steroids before each infusion to help prevent reactions. Your care team will monitor you closely during and for at least an hour after each infusion.
